name: Standard Scramble
approach: Start at the Entiat River Trailhead (elev. ~3,150 ft) at the end of Entiat River Road (FS Road 51), where a Northwest Forest Pass is required. Follow the Entiat River Trail No. 1400 upstream through mixed forest along the river's south bank, gently graded, for about 4 miles. At roughly the 4-mile mark the trail reaches the crossing where a footbridge once stood; the bridge deck burned in the 2015 Wolverine Fire and only the steel I-beams and railing remain, so plan on either crab-walking the exposed beams (some real fall risk, especially with a pack) or fording the Entiat River directly, which can run high and cold with early-season snowmelt — this crossing is the approach's main hazard and should be scouted before committing. Once across, pick up the Cow Creek Meadows Trail No. 1404 and climb steadily northwest through subalpine forest, passing the Myrtle Lake spur (about 0.4-0.5 mile off-trail to the lake, a good water source and camp option) around the 5-mile mark. Continue up-valley into Cow Creek Meadows itself (roughly 6,000-6,300 ft), an open avalanche-prone basin below the Fifth of July Mountain ridgeline — snow can linger here into July and avalanche debris/downed timber from the slopes above is common, so expect some route-finding through blowdown and brush at the meadow's edges. From Cow Creek Meadows, leave the maintained trail and work up open talus and heather slopes on the mountain's south side toward the south ridge/saddle, gaining the final ~1,400-1,600 ft cross-country over scree, boulders and intermittent goat/climber's paths. There is no reliable water above Cow Creek Meadows, so fill up there or at Myrtle Lake. Total one-way distance to the summit is on the order of 8-9 miles with about 4,500 ft of gain, consistent with a long day trip or, more commonly, an overnight basecamp at Myrtle Lake, Cow Creek Meadows, or the Larch Lakes.
descent_text: Descend by reversing the ascent line: pick your way back down the open south-facing talus, scree and heather slopes off the south ridge/saddle to Cow Creek Meadows, watching footing on the loose rock (more hazardous descending than climbing) and staying alert for parties below if scree is being kicked loose. From the meadows, drop back onto Cow Creek Meadows Trail No. 1404, pass the Myrtle Lake spur, and rejoin the Entiat River Trail No. 1400 for the roughly 4-mile walk back down-valley to the trailhead. The Entiat River crossing near the old bridge site (burned I-beams or a ford) is again the key obstacle and is often trickier tired and later in the day when snowmelt flows are higher. This is a walk-off/scramble descent with no technical downclimbing and no rappels required under normal summer conditions; a helmet is worth carrying for the loose south-slope terrain, and an ice axe may be prudent for early-season snow patches on the upper mountain or in Cow Creek Meadows.

itinerary.cal: Trail #1404 through Cow Creek Meadows is steep and can hold snow into July; the classic season is Aug-Sept for open meadows or late Sept/early Oct for larch color, and this is self-issue wilderness permit country (Glacier Peak Wilderness) with no reservation needed.

days.note: From the Entiat River Trailhead (~3,150 ft), follow Entiat River Trail #1400 north about 4 gentle miles along the river to the Cow Creek Meadows Trail #1404 junction and footbridge, then climb 0.4-0.9 mi to established camps on the south shore of Myrtle Lake (~3,750 ft). Most parties treat this as an easy half-day and spend the afternoon scouting the route into Cow Creek Meadows.
days.title: Hike in to Myrtle Lake / Cow Creek Meadows
days.objective: Establish camp for the summit push

days.note: Leave the maintained Trail #1404 above Cow Creek Meadows and climb open slopes/talus on the south side and south ridge to the summit — straightforward Class 1-2 scrambling with big Glacier Peak Wilderness views. Many parties tack on a visit to Cow Creek Pass and the Larch Lakes basin on the same day since the terrain is open and connected.
days.title: Summit day: Cow Creek Meadows to Fifth of July Mountain

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Light day pack, hike back up Trail #1404 toward Cow Creek Meadows.

schedule.label: Leave the maintained trail
schedule.detail: Enter open meadows/talus and begin the off-trail climb up the south slopes.

schedule.label: Reach the summit ridge / top out
schedule.detail: 7,696 ft summit; wide views toward the Entiat Mountains and Glacier Peak.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Reverse the ascent line back to Cow Creek Meadows.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Optional afternoon side trip toward Cow Creek Pass/Larch Lakes for parties with energy left.

days.objective: Reach the 7,696 ft summit and return to camp

days.note: Retrace Trail #1404 down to the Trail #1400 junction and follow the Entiat River Trail back to the trailhead.
days.title: Hike out

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day, ~16-18 mile round trip with about 4,400-4,500 ft total gain; most parties backpack in to Myrtle Lake or Cow Creek Meadows and make the summit a day trip from camp, often combined with Cow Creek Pass and Larch Lakes.
